title: listing
description: A store listing: settlement value S, stock, redemption policy.

businessId.description: NOT required: TASKS.md 9.2.a's staff moderation routes (`approve_listing`/`reject_listing`/`view`, ops-only) name no single business in their URL, same reasoning as voucher_batch.json's own comment. Cerbos runs with enforcement: reject, so requiring it would fail schema validation, and therefore deny, every staff listing-moderation route before any rule ran. Every business-side route still supplies it via the tenant path (`PdpGuard`'s own `businessId: tenantId`) unaffected -- this only stops an ABSENT value from being refused before the rules below run.

isMaterialSettlementDecrease.description: True when the proposed change lowers S at all. There is NO threshold: founder decision 2026-09-21 (YT-0576) removed the invented 20% placeholder rather than ratifying it, because a threshold creates a band below the line that is reachable repeatedly -- two 15% cuts under a 20% threshold take S down 27.75% with nobody approving anything. Computed in apps/api/src/modules/store/material-settlement-decrease.ts, which needs the STORED S, so this attribute cannot be supplied by attrsFrom alone. Deliberately NOT in `required`: required applies to the resource kind, not one action, so requiring it refuses approve_settlement_decrease -- which carries no materiality flag -- before any rule runs. That was tried and reverted after turning Integration red on three commits. docs/17 section 2.1 makes this one of the three two-person-approval actions.

requestedBy.description: Principal who raised the change. The approver must not be this person.

region.description: 1.5.b's F2 hard wall: the business's own region, compared against P.attr.jurisdiction.

audience.description: 12.1.b's audience-targeting wall for the `browse` action (StoreCatalogueController) -- same status as campaign_view.json's own `audience`. Not required: every WRITE action on this kind (create/edit/set_settlement_value/...) never populates it, and requiring it would refuse those before any rule ran, same reasoning as `businessId` above.
